title: The scary first year
topic: Falls and the time to wait

messages.text: Have you looked at Mia's fund? It's down 20%
€5,000 is now €4,000. Sell before it gets worse?
She needs it in 17 years, not next week

steps.prompt: After a fall, the price must rise more than it fell to get back. Find the loss that needs a +25% rise.

goal.hint: It's the loss Mia's fund just had.

steps.prompt: The fund part is at €4,000 after one bad year. What does Lena do? Jump to Mia's 18th birthday.

choices.label: Sell now and keep it as cash
choices.ending: €5,100 at 18. Selling turned a fall on paper into a real loss, and the cash then barely kept up with prices.

choices.label: Hold and look less often
choices.ending: €11,800 at 18, after a first year nobody enjoyed. In this path the market recovered. Past returns promise nothing about the next 17 years.

choices.label: If she had never started
choices.ending: €6,400 at 18. Calm all the way, and smaller. Not wrong, a different trade: less worry for less growth.

steps.title: A fall is a price, not a verdict
steps.body: [[volatility|Swings]] are the price of growth that isn't guaranteed. What makes a fall dangerous is having to sell during it. That's why the [[time-horizon]] decides which money can sit in something that falls. Simplified from real data.

steps.prompt: Why does a −20% year hurt Mia's money less than it would hurt next month's rent?
options: Mia's money has 17 years to recover and nobody needs to sell it now
steps.explanation: Rent money would have to be sold at the low point. Money that can wait has time for the price to climb back, though nothing guarantees it will.

steps.prompt: The fund fell 20%. What rise brings it back to the start?
steps.explanation: €4,000 × 1.25 = €5,000. The rise is taken from the smaller amount, so it has to be bigger than the fall.

messages.text: Did you see Mia's fund? It went down 20%
She needs it in 17 years, not next week
I know. It still feels bad

s1.prompt: When a price falls, it must rise more than it fell to get back. Find the loss that needs +25% to get back.

output.label: How much it must go up

sc1.prompt: After one bad year the fund is worth €4,000. What does Lena do? See what happens when Mia is 18.

choices.label: Sell now and keep cash
choices.ending: €5,100 at 18. Selling made the loss real. Then the cash grew very slowly.

choices.label: Keep it and check less often
choices.ending: €11,800 at 18. In this example the market came back. The future can be different.

choices.label: Never start at all
choices.ending: €6,400 at 18. No stress, and less money. A different choice, not a wrong one.

t1.title: Going down is normal
t1.body: Prices go up and down. This is [[volatility]]. The problem is when you must sell while the price is down. So how long money can wait, the [[time-horizon]], decides where it can go.

q1.prompt: Why is a −20% year less bad for Mia's money than for rent money?
options: Mia's money can wait 17 years, nobody must sell it now
q1.explanation: Rent money must be used now, at the low price. Money that can wait has time to come back, but there is no promise.

q2.prompt: The fund went down 20%. How much must it go up to get back?
q2.explanation: €4,000 × 1.25 = €5,000. It must go up more than it went down.
